A goal is accepted by its sponsor when the sponsor is a person and by an operator when an agent sponsors it, after its sponsor activated it, relying on its current evaluation, which finds every condition met, and never by that evaluation's author or by the author of one of its steps.

Read by release 0.4.2, the first published release to read it, and later (0.4.0, which introduced it, was withdrawn).

types.name: product
types.summary: A product the estate owns: name, summary, editions and surfaces, and optionally how its releases are made (the destination and the artifacts a complete release carries). Details live in design documents.

fields.description: The platform profile, as design/platforms.md names it, for example linux-x64 or Workbench on macOS.

types.name: qualification
types.summary: A platform profile's qualification for a release, derived from its observations and never asserted beside them: qualified, measured in part, not qualified, or a non-claim, with the verifications, reviews and observations it rests on and what they do not establish.

fields.description: The successor of the subject that remains current, or the chosen first communication profile at that scope.
fields.name: kept

fields.name: note

fields.description: Exact bounded grant used to reconcile policy or exception history; no generic engineering grant substitutes.
fields.name: policyAuthority

types.name: reconciliation
types.summary: Settles divergent revisions of one record by keeping one successor and withdrawing the others. Communication scopes also permit their owner to settle independent first profiles at that exact scope. Nothing is deleted.

types.name: release
types.summary: An identified release of a product: version, exact commit, artifacts by hash and platform, software bill of materials, notices, evidence, record-format compatibility, signing state, limitations and status. A candidate precedes publication; a published revision supersedes it after the operator's acceptance and the observed publication.

types.name: result
types.summary: What an attempt submits: outcome, summary, outputs by hash, evidence, checks performed or not, limitations, unresolved external effects and the next permitted step. A claim to inspect; acceptance is a separate record pinned to this exact result.

types.name: retirement
types.summary: Registers a temporary artifact (path) with the condition for its removal; once retiredAt is set the path must be gone.

fields.description: self when the reviewer authored the subject; independent-agent for a different agent principal; operator for the operator.
fields.name: independence

fields.description: The verdict.

fields.description: What was reviewed and how.
fields.name: summary

fields.name: findings

fields.description: For a review of a goal, its evaluation, and only then: one entry per completion condition in the goal's order, each a verdict (met|not-yet|impossible), the reason and the records it read ({type, id, hash}); the outcome is pass when every verdict is met, fail when one is impossible, and findings otherwise.
fields.name: conditions

fields.description: Unique exact evidence references for an ordinary result review; duty reviews require an admitted-device signature.
fields.name: read

types.name: review
types.summary: A review of an exact subject revision. Independence is checked against who authored the subject: self, independent-agent or operator. A review of a goal is its evaluation: a verdict on each completion condition with the records it read, by a principal who authored none of the goal's steps.

fields.description: Explicit execution choices and cumulative restrictions; launcher, roster, goal, assignment, then run precedence. Role restrictions remain binding.
fields.name: execution

fields.description: stallSeconds (event-stream silence limit, 1–86400 seconds) and watch (bounded rate and loop thresholds), inherited by goals using this roster. Goal fields override these; omitted fields keep the launcher defaults.
fields.name: limits

types.name: roster
types.summary: Who fills each role of the estate's work, in order of preference: planner, builder, reviewer, evaluator, release manager, publisher and decider, or a role the estate names. Agents where available, people where needed; a role with no available principal becomes an ask, never a silent fallback.

types.name: verification
types.summary: A check of an exact subject (a repository resource, a result or a release) at an exact commit: the method, the command, the environment, who performed it, the observed result, evidence and limitations. Evidence, never permission; historical once the subject changes.

fields.description: Short upper-case key such as M0 or DESIGN-01; unique among current work orders.

types.name: work-progress
types.summary: The contributor's claim about one completed phase of an attempt. At most one record per phase; interim notes stay in live state. Neither liveness nor acceptance.

types.name: work-status
